clue.text: Anger gripping almost all in French train

indicators.note: to grip something is to hold it inside, so the first word goes around the next piece
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the French word is dropped

blocks.note: to anger someone is to enrage them
tout is French for all

explanation.surface: Someone fumes while nearly everyone on a French railway carriage looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway train, but it is the retinue that follows a dignitary; 'in French' tells you the word for all is French.
explanation.definitionFit: A train in the older sense is a group of attendants following an important person, which is exactly an entourage.

clue.text: Characteristic spirit of English chap lacking master’s degree

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the degree's letters are taken out of the name

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
a man's name standing for any chap
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: An Englishman without a postgraduate qualification still has a certain character about him.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos means the distinctive guiding beliefs and character of a person, group or culture.

clue.text: Northern boatmen circulating completely naturally

indicators.note: circulating means moving around, so the letters of the preceding words are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words used as fodder

explanation.surface: Boatmen from the north of England mill about doing what comes to them without effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from Hamlet, describes doing something as if born to it, with innate ease and no training needed.

clue.text: Disturbance at university over fellow introducing a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the rest
introducing means bringing in next, so the following pieces come straight after

blocks.note: up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford
a fellow is a male, he
taken as written
Val is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A student causes a commotion by bringing a young woman into college.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at university is a British usage for being in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: An upheaval is a violent or sudden change causing great disruption, a synonym for a disturbance.

clue.text: Cause of discomfort, one involving head, principally

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap in, so the word for one encloses the other piece
principally points at the leading part, so only the opening letter of the word before it is used

blocks.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
the first letter of head

explanation.surface: Something hurts, and the trouble seems mostly to be in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a headache; the H slips inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a continuous dull pain, something that causes physical discomfort.

clue.text: Welshman takes time welcoming key priest and preacher

indicators.note: takes means adds on, so the next piece is attached after the name
to welcome is to receive inside, so the outer letters wrap around the following pieces

blocks.note: Evans is a typically Welsh surname
T is the abbreviation for time
G is a musical key
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A Welsh minister takes his time showing a fellow cleric into the chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' here is a musical key, not something that opens a door; the Welshman is the common Welsh surname, not a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist is someone who preaches the gospel, often travelling to spread the Christian message.

clue.text: Impudent, but shy about certain knowledge at first

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for shy goes round the other piece
at first points at the opening letters of the words before it

blocks.note: coy means bashful or shy
the first letters of certain and knowledge

explanation.surface: A person is cheeky yet bashful whenever sure of the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocky describes someone conceited and overconfident in a cheeky way, close to impudent or brash.

clue.text: Salad ingredient offered by engineer on the French railway

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after, so the pieces follow in sequence

blocks.note: CE stands for civil engineer
le is a French word for the
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: An engineer hands out salad on a train in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Celery is a crunchy green vegetable whose stalks are commonly eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Disputable nature of material is absorbing old university head

indicators.note: to absorb is to take inside, so the little word surrounds the next pieces

blocks.note: content is the material of a book or website
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old
U is the abbreviation for university
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Arguments arise over the course content involving an elderly college principal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a university head, but it is a headland, NESS; IS takes in O and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Contentiousness is the quality of being likely to cause argument, so a nature open to dispute.

clue.text: You once strayed badly, very recently

indicators.note: badly means done wrong, so the letters of the word before it end up in the wrong order

blocks.note: ye is the archaic form of you
the letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that only a short while ago you went off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' looks like a time word, but it signals the old form YE.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday as an adverb can mean in the recent past, not literally the day before, so very lately.

clue.text: Make a splash with popular show the boss scores

blocks.note: a popular show is a hit
taken as written
the boss is the head of an organisation
a score is a line scratched or cut into a surface

explanation.surface: A hit musical earns rave reviews and the producer chalks up a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' suggests points or music, but here it means marks scratched into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a splash is to attract widespread public attention, as a story featured prominently in newspapers does.

clue.text: Observed at Ely perhaps, it has its ups and downs

definitions.text: it has its ups and downs

indicators.note: at means placed beside, so the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: Ely is a cathedral city and so a bishop's see; perhaps marks it as one example
observed means saw

explanation.surface: Something was spotted at Ely that goes through good times and bad.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is the seat of a bishop, and Ely in Cambridgeshire is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a plank on a pivot that children ride, each end rising and falling in turn.

clue.text: Upset a Rhode Island girl carrying goods

indicators.note: to carry is to hold within, so the opening pieces take the last one inside

blocks.note: taken as written
RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island
Eve is a girl's name
G is short for good, so two goods are GG

explanation.surface: A young woman from Rhode Island is distressed while lugging her merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: GG goes in straight after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to cause someone distress or resentment by treating them unfairly, so to upset them.

clue.text: Amateur poet touring India with native of Latvia

indicators.note: to tour is to go all around, so the poet's name surrounds the other pieces

blocks.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a Lett is a Latvian

explanation.surface: An unpaid versifier travels round India with a companion from Latvia.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in an art or subject without professional commitment, just as an amateur does.

clue.text: Daughter leaves older relative badly needing a piece of fruit

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so that letter departs from the relative's word
needing means requiring something extra, so the further pieces are added after

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
a grandad is an older relative
ill means badly, as in ill-treated
taken as written

explanation.surface: A daughter walks out on her ailing grandparent, who needs something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing a D from GRANDAD leaves GRANAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The granadilla is the edible fruit of certain passion-flower species, eaten as a piece of fruit.

clue.text: Restrict online messages — and entrance supporters?

blocks.note: to gate a pupil is to confine them to school as a punishment
messages put up online are posts

explanation.surface: Someone wants to clamp down on internet chatter, and wonders who backs the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: To gate is British school slang for confining a pupil to the grounds; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateposts hold up a gate, so they literally support the way in to a field or garden.

clue.text: Endlessly examine horses kept for breeding

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter of the next word goes

blocks.note: to study is to examine closely

explanation.surface: Someone keeps scrutinising the breeding stallions at a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a group of horses, or an establishment, kept for breeding purposes.

clue.text: Pays to register for arduous trek

blocks.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
to log is to record or register

explanation.surface: A hiker pays a fee to sign up for a gruelling walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A footslog is a long tiring march or hike on foot, the kind of laborious journey a trek is.

clue.text: One maintaining pianos, you say? Something fishy here

indicators.note: you say points to how a word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: a piano tuner keeps pianos in order; in non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same

explanation.surface: Someone suspects the piano repairer is up to something dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something fishy' sounds like suspicion, but it is literally a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large sea fish, so it is quite literally something fishy.

clue.text: My soil goes shaky? This might explain it

definitions.text: My soil goes shaky? This might explain it

indicators.note: shaky means unsteady, so the letters before it are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of all three words used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone feels the ground trembling beneath them and asks what science could account for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the shaking ground is an earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismology is the scientific study of earthquakes, the discipline that explains why the ground trembles.

clue.text: Group once fashionable — a little

blocks.note: hep is a dated form of hip, meaning trendy
a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: A band that used to be trendy has faded a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptad is a set or group of seven things, from the Greek word for seven.

clue.text: Pass through some super meat extract

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the answer is a portion of the following words

blocks.note: running across the end of super, all of meat and the start of extract

explanation.surface: A tasty beef concentrate soaks right through whatever it touches.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate is to spread throughout or seep into something, passing through every part of it.

clue.text: Way a little sibling defines stagnation

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written
sis is short for sister, so a shortened sibling

explanation.surface: A younger brother or sister's lifestyle is summed up as going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' looks like younger, but it means the shortened word SIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state where nothing changes or develops, which is the same as stagnation.

clue.text: Less confident breed of horse, do we hear?

indicators.note: do we hear asks the solver to listen, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a shire is a large English draught horse breed

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a particular breed of horse is more timid than others.
explanation.definitionFit: Shyer is the comparative of shy, meaning more timid and so having less self-assurance.

clue.text: Fever absent-minded vicar initially escapes

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the word before it
escapes means gets out, so that letter leaves the earlier word

blocks.note: someone absent-minded is vague
the first letter of vicar

explanation.surface: A forgetful clergyman manages to avoid catching a temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for a malarial fever with bouts of shivering and sweating.

clue.text: Filming part of theatre where reports may be heard

blocks.note: shooting a film is filming it
the gallery is the highest seating area in a theatre

explanation.surface: A film crew is at work in the upper tier of a theatre where news is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reports' looks like news stories, but they are the bangs of guns.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting gallery is a place for target practice, where the sharp sounds of gunshots ring out.

clue.text: Assume extremists for years have backed council

indicators.note: extremists means the letters at the two ends, applied to the word that follows
backed means moved backwards, so the joined letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: to don clothing is to assume or put it on
the first and last letters of years

explanation.surface: Hardliners have long supported the local governing body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' sounds political, but it means the end letters of years.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church clergy and officials, a governing council of a church.

clue.text: It peps up one tucking into fresh greens with hesitation

indicators.note: tucking into means placed inside, so that letter goes into the jumbled word
fresh means made anew, so the following word is remade in a different order
with means alongside, so the last piece is added at the end

blocks.note: the letters used as fodder
I is the Roman numeral one
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Somebody reluctantly digs into a plate of fresh vegetables that will give them a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: An energiser is anything that invigorates or gives vitality, so something that perks a person up.
